A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BNRM research, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model training and evaluation, PPO policy evaluations, noise and data-size experiments, debiasing analyses, and Best-of-N results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Arena-Hard judgments, human assessments, training-time measurements, and factor-stability results.

M1.justification: The local/global non-negative reward factorization, Gamma priors, Weibull variational inference, KL-regularized objective, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added appendix arguments explain and analyze the existing method rather than introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds Arena-Hard-v0.1 prompts for evaluating generated-response preferences, supplementing the existing reward benchmarks and downstream capability tasks. The factor-stability study reuses existing model and dataset coverage. Multi-turn, tool-use, and long-horizon scenarios are discussed as future work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: New Table 4 compares the BNRM-aligned policy against base Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct. Mistral is newly used as a response-policy opponent; the earlier Mistral-based gold reward model served as an evaluator. Comparator membership in the retained reward-model and PPO tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a materially different validation protocol: GPT-4.1 pairwise judgments and blind assessment of 50 randomly sampled Arena-Hard pairs by two experts, reporting win/tie/loss rates. It also adds factor comparisons across backbones and training datasets and a full-fine-tuning timing comparison. Existing training settings remain unchanged in v1 Table 6/v2 Table 9.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a focused test of whether factor semantics recur across runs, backbones, and datasets, plus measured training overhead in Tables 6–7. Earlier noise, KL-sensitivity, convergence, debiasing, and Best-of-N analyses are retained. Expanded explanations of those retained analyses do not establish additional experiments.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly reports factor correspondences for the main run and two additional runs, described in Appendix A.3 as using different random seeds. This adds repeated-run reporting for interpretability, without establishing additional repetitions of the earlier accuracy experiments. Confidence intervals and quantitative uncertainty estimates are not added.

E6.justification: New results include Arena-Hard GPT-4.1 outcomes, human-average win/tie/loss rates of 51%/18%/31%, training times, and factor correspondences. Table 2 revises Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B's average from 92.5 to 93.1 while BNRM remains 93.6, shrinking its reported advantage from 1.1 to 0.5 points. Most earlier numerical results and plotted trends are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces an NMF formulation, selective-window and sparsity conditions, and a claimed uniqueness guarantee up to permutation and scaling. Appendix D adds a sparsity/incoherence-based generalization bound in Equation 11. These substantially extend v1's mathematical content, although the PDF does not demonstrate the required conditions or provide a complete derivation of the bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims: Bayesian non-negative reward factorization, scalable Weibull inference, and improved robustness, interpretability, and generalization. New evaluations and appendix arguments support or elaborate these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations concerning factor reproducibility, preserved expressiveness, minimal hyperparameter tuning, computational scalability, and resistance to open-ended reward hacking. It interprets the human evaluation as evidence beyond proxy rewards. New limitations acknowledge KL-coefficient tuning and untested multi-turn, tool-use, and long-horizon settings.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 adds a code-access URL. New Appendix C.2 specifies uniformly selecting floor(N × noise ratio) preference pairs and swapping their labels, clarifying an existing experiment rather than establishing a changed corruption procedure. Table 6 adds wall-clock training times; the earlier algorithm, software descriptions, and hyperparameter table are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Arena-Hard evaluation, NMF identifiability, sparse-coding bounds, linear representations, and deep non-negative models. Appendix A.4 expands the comparison with the already-cited InfoRM. The central positioning remains unchanged; duplicate or publication-version reference changes do not constitute new research relationships.

P1.justification: The original narrative is largely retained. v2 inserts Appendix A.3–A.5, moves the former A.3 to A.6, expands the sensitivity discussion, and adds limitations, acknowledgements, and an impact statement. It also makes localized terminology, affiliation, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for Arena-Hard/human evaluation, training time, and factor stability, while relocating and renumbering retained displays. Figure 7's KL-coefficient label changes from lambda to eta without changing its curves. The existing diagrams, plots, and table designs otherwise remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the human evaluation, factor-stability checks, measured overhead, and reproducibility disclosures provide useful additional evidence. However, v2 introduces uniqueness and distribution-shift guarantees without establishing their assumptions or derivations, and its claim that all seven semantic families recur across every setting exceeds Table 7's reported matches. These empirical benefits and new overstatements materially pull quality in opposite directions, preventing a reliable net improvement judgment.
